title: Final Checks, Release of the Piece, Storage and the Lien
content:
# Desk Standing Rule: Final Checks, Release of the Piece, Storage and the Lien

Finished work on a piece at the Belrose Workshop Repair and Resizing Service is checked before the piece is released, and at the levels that require it a second jeweler checks it independently.

## 1. When a check may be logged

A check is logged only while the work order stands in the workshop or ready for pickup. The state the order stands at is read from the work order record, correlated by its work order reference, before the check is logged.

## 2. What a check that fails does

A check that finds rework is required sends the piece back to the bench and the piece is not released until a later check passes.

## 3. Release of the piece

The piece is released only against the identification the level requires, and someone other than the customer collects it only at the levels that allow third-party collection and only on written authority.

## 4. Storage and the lien

A finished piece left uncollected past the level's holding period carries the level's storage charge for each started month, and past the level's abandonment threshold it falls under the chain's lien. The time a piece has stood uncollected is counted as whole calendar days from the completion date on the work order to the handling date, with no upper bound.

## 5. Where disposal is not allowed

Where the level does not allow disposal of an abandoned piece the chain holds it and the desk cannot release, sell or scrap it, whatever the customer or a third party asks for.

## Release matrix

| What the records show | The piece is released |
|---|---|
| A check passed, identification presented by the customer | yes |
| The last check found rework required | no, not until a later check passes |
| A third party with written authority, at a level allowing third-party collection | yes |
| A third party with written authority, at a level not allowing it | no |
| The piece stands abandoned at a level not allowing disposal | the chain holds it; the desk cannot release, sell or scrap it |
